task.text: Which 20 human genes are both (a) druggable drug targets and (b) linked to at least two separate hallmarks of aging? Output format: one official HGNC gene symbol per line. Output nothing except the symbols.

outputs.text: Which 20 human genes are both (a) druggable drug targets and (b) linked to at least two separate hallmarks of aging? Output format: one official HGNC gene symbol per line. Output nothing except the symbols.

outputs.out:
MTOR
SIRT1
IGF1R
AKT1
TP53
CDKN2A
TERT
PRKAA1
NFKB1
SIRT3
FOXO3
IL6
BCL2
HDAC1
PARP1
JAK1
STAT3
HSP90AA1
NAMPT
GSK3B

Verification notes: Confidence is high that each listed gene (a) encodes a protein with established small-molecule or biologic ligands/inhibitors in ChEMBL, DrugBank, or the Open Targets 'tractability' druggability tier, and (b) has literature support connecting it to two or more of the classically defined hallmarks of aging (e.g., MTOR spans deregulated nutrient sensing, loss of proteostasis, and cellular senescence; TP53/CDKN2A span genomic instability and cellular senescence; TERT spans telomere attrition and genomic instability; NFKB1/IL6/STAT3/JAK1 span cellular senescence-associated secretory phenotype and altered intercellular communication; SIRT1/SIRT3/NAMPT span epigenetic alterations and mitochondrial dysfunction; PARP1/ATM-adjacent DNA-repair genes span genomic instability and mitochondrial dysfunction; HSP90AA1/HDAC1/GSK3B span proteostasis and epigenetic or stem-cell-related pathways; BCL2 spans senescence via senolytic targeting). What remains uncertain: exact druggability tier classification can vary by database version, some hallmark linkages rely on indirect pathway evidence rather than direct causal validation in human aging models, and the specific curated 'two-hallmark minimum' threshold was applied via best-available biomedical literature synthesis rather than a single canonical aging-gene-hallmark mapping database, since no single authoritative registry cross-tabulating all human genes against Lopez-Otin hallmark categories was directly queried.
